topic: Rational common-law certificates for simultaneous effects across sparsest causal graphs. Input finite variables, an exact CI bit-vector, background orientations, and the explicitly enumerated minimum-edge SA-MPDAG/CPDAG I-maps with certificates. For a fixed query P_x(Y), expand each represented DAG's truncated factorization into rational observed-table polynomials. Saturate the common CI ideal by all positive cells and denominators and use fixed-order real-radical normal forms for sound equality certificates. Prove SparseSIM-ID complete on this tied sparsest family: it returns either one common observable arithmetic circuit with checkable real-Nullstellensatz certificates, or two represented DAGs and a strictly positive rational table satisfying every oracle/graph restriction but giving different intervention laws. The hard theorem is effect-specific rational-positive separation for the common-law model; generic radical decision is supporting machinery. Give explicit termination/certificate bounds and plug-in inference after common identification. Consumer: Tetrad SP and causaldag/GSP all-ties output should report a common effect or a concrete ambiguity table instead of selecting one tied graph. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: An explicit separator lemma was derived for oppositely oriented oracle-inseparable binary edges. Exact enumeration of all 543 four-variable DAGs for the rational law (4,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,1,4,1,1,4,4)/40 found exactly four elementary CIs, 50 I-maps, and exactly two four-edge minimum DAGs in distinct MECs; their do(1=+1) effect on variable 3 is 13/20 versus 1/2. Checks exposed that graph-Markov constraints are redundant given the exact I-map oracle and that saturation alone does not encode strict positivity; no counterexample or prior-art completion of the general causal completeness theorem was found. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Prove that every intervention cross-product outside the rational real radical of the declared saturated oracle ideal has a strictly positive rational common-law point separating the effect for the tied minimum-edge family. EARLY KILL TEST: On positive rational binary four-variable multi-MEC oracles, enumerate all I-map DAGs and singleton-effect queries, then compare nonzero saturated-real-radical remainders with exact positive feasibility of F!=0; one nonzero remainder with no positive separator kills K1--K2. STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/scm_sparsestfamily_simid_complete.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Is there a necessary-and-sufficient terminating certificate procedure for simultaneous identification of P_x(Y) over every minimum-edge SA-MPDAG/CPDAG I-map of one exact finite CI oracle, returning either a common rational observed-law functional or a strictly positive rational common-law separator?

source_refs.claim: The paper proves only a sufficient simultaneous-identification criterion; its necessity discussion requires a density Markov to every candidate graph with unequal effects and identifies least-edge SP outputs as a structured candidate family.
source_refs.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, Terry Soo
source_refs.venue: ICML 2025 Workshop on Scaling Up Intervention Models

source_refs.claim: The sparsest-permutation method targets minimum-edge permutation DAGs under the sparsest Markov representation assumption, but does not define an effect-commonness decision for ties spanning distinct MECs.
source_refs.author: Garvesh Raskutti, Caroline Uhler

source_refs.claim: The paper represents discrete Bayesian-network conditional independences through polynomial ideals and algebraic varieties, without comparing intervention functionals across several observationally compatible graphs.
source_refs.author: Luis David Garcia, Michael Stillman, Bernd Sturmfels

open_problems.why_unsolved: Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo reduce simultaneous identification to a sufficient graphical condition but explicitly leave necessity open because failure must be witnessed by one density compatible with all candidate graphs that separates two graph-specific interventions. Restricting candidates to tied minimum-edge I-maps supplies additional combinatorial structure, but existing work does not connect non-equality of rational truncated-factorization expressions modulo a common CI model to a strictly positive rational separating point. CI ideals describe algebraic closures, whereas positivity, denominator nonvanishing, and exact non-CI assertions are semialgebraic open conditions; saturation alone neither supplies that bridge nor bounds rational witness size.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A completeness theorem and terminating algorithm with explicit degree and bit-complexity bounds that outputs either one rational arithmetic circuit with checkable real-Nullstellensatz equality certificates for every represented DAG or two represented DAGs and a bounded-bit strictly positive rational table realizing the exact oracle and separating P_x(Y).

writing_exemplar.why: Its framing moves directly from failure to isolate one MEC to effect-specific agreement across a candidate graph family, and its discussion states the shared-density necessity obstacle.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: observational discovery can return several defensible MECs -> selecting one graph is unjustified -> the causal effect may nevertheless be common -> decide completeness by returning either a shared functional or a common-law separator

method_exemplars.technique: Use proper possibly causal paths and partial-causal-order bucket factorization to obtain graph-specific generalized truncated-factorization functionals, then cross-multiply those rational expressions.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies the graph-specific observable functional whose equality must be certified across every tied SA-MPDAG.

method_exemplars.technique: Encode discrete CI restrictions as determinantal polynomial ideals and use elimination and component decomposition to isolate probabilistically relevant components.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested theorem asks whether cross-products of graph-specific intervention formulas vanish on the positive component of a common discrete CI variety.

method_exemplars.technique: Resample intermediate CI statistics, screen candidate graphs, aggregate graph-specific estimates, and prove coverage through a simultaneous graph-retention event.
method_exemplars.why_closest: After common identification is certified, the same discovery-uncertainty machinery can support inference while replacing a conservative union of distinct graphwise targets by one certified shared target.

open_problems.open_problem: Can minimum-edge I-map DAGs of an exact CI oracle be partitioned output-sensitively into maximal classes whose P_x(Y) rational functionals agree on the strictly positive common-law model, without enumerating every DAG or treating syntactically different formulas as distinct effects?

source_refs.claim: The paper minimally enumerates distinct total-effect functionals within one MPDAG by recursively adding orientations, but does not cover candidates in different MECs or equality only modulo their common observational constraints.
source_refs.author: F. Richard Guo, Emilija Perković

source_refs.claim: The paper gives linear-delay enumeration of DAGs in one MEC and extends enumeration to MPDAGs with background knowledge, but does not quotient outputs by causal-effect equality.
source_refs.author: Marcel Wienöbst, Malte Luttermann, Max Bannach, Maciej Liśkiewicz

source_refs.claim: The paper studies simultaneous identification over non-Markov-equivalent SA-MPDAGs but gives a pairwise sufficient condition rather than a minimal effect quotient or output-sensitive enumeration procedure.
source_refs.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, Terry Soo
source_refs.venue: ICML 2025 Workshop on Scaling Up Intervention Models

open_problems.why_unsolved: Guo and Perković collapse duplicate effect formulas only inside the DAG class represented by one MPDAG, where a recursive orientation invariant is available. Tied sparsest I-maps may lie in distinct MECs, and two truncated-factorization expressions may become equal only after imposing their shared oracle CIs, making syntactic comparison incomplete. Wienöbst et al. enumerate graph structures rather than equivalence classes modulo an effect ideal. The first proof step that must change is the orientation-recursion invariant: it must carry a canonical effect normal form modulo the positive common-law model while graph transitions may cross MEC boundaries; the web scan found no existing method occupying that target-method pair.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An output-sensitive algorithm and complexity theorem producing one certified representative circuit for each maximal common-law effect class of minimum-edge I-map DAGs, with delay polynomial in graph size and algebraic-certificate size and with no duplicate effect classes.

writing_exemplar.why: Its problem formulation makes duplicate causal effects, rather than duplicate DAGs, the computational object and motivates a minimal effect-aware output.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: an equivalence-class graph may represent exponentially many DAGs -> DAGwise effect enumeration repeats identical functionals -> query-relevant orientations remove duplicates -> extend effect-minimal enumeration across tied sparsest MECs and modulo their shared CI law

method_exemplars.technique: Recursively orient query-relevant edges and prove that each emitted MPDAG subclass has one identified functional and that distinct outputs do not duplicate it.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired output is the same query-specific quotient, with equality strengthened from one-MPDAG graphical equality to algebraic equality across several MECs.

method_exemplars.technique: Traverse represented DAGs with linear delay using local orientation updates and bounded structural Hamming distance between consecutive outputs.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Local graph transitions provide an enumeration backbone on which effect-normal-form caching and cross-MEC quotienting can be layered.

method_exemplars.technique: Attach recursive least-squares estimators to MPDAG-identified total-effect functionals and prove efficiency among regular covariance-based estimators under linearity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how a common effect class can receive a concrete estimator and limit-theory rung instead of separately estimating every represented DAG, while making its additional linear-model restriction explicit.

open_problems.open_problem: What is the sharp identified range of P_x(Y), or of pairwise intervention disagreement, over strictly positive finite distributions realizing an exact CI oracle and over all of its minimum-edge I-map DAGs when simultaneous point identification fails?

source_refs.claim: Autobounds compiles a discrete causal query under a specified causal model and evidence into a polynomial program whose extrema are sharp and whose incomplete optimization has anytime validity and epsilon-sharpness guarantees.
source_refs.author: Guilherme Duarte, Noam Finkelstein, Dean Knox, Jonathan Mummolo, Ilya Shpitser
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: When a total effect is unidentified in one MPDAG, the paper enumerates distinct observable effect functionals but does not optimize their disagreement over distributions shared by several MECs.
source_refs.author: F. Richard Guo, Emilija Perković

source_refs.claim: The paper studies a yes-or-no common-effect question across several candidate SA-MPDAGs; outside its sufficient conditions it neither gives sharp effect bounds nor quantifies worst-case disagreement on the common-law model.
source_refs.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, Terry Soo
source_refs.venue: ICML 2025 Workshop on Scaling Up Intervention Models

open_problems.why_unsolved: Existing strands address separate pieces: Guo and Perković enumerate graph-induced functionals within one MPDAG, Teh et al. give sufficient conditions for their equality across several SA-MPDAGs, and Duarte et al. optimize a polynomialized query under one declared discrete causal model. Direct composition fails because the feasible set here is a strictly positive shared observational-law model constrained by an exact CI oracle, while each graph contributes a different rational truncated factorization. Autobounds' initial parameterization must be replaced by shared observed-table variables linked to all candidate graphs, with non-CIs and strict positivity retained rather than silently closed.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A sharp-bound theorem and certified optimization procedure returning the exact infimum and supremum of every graphwise P_x(Y), or the maximal pairwise gap, over the positive exact-oracle model, together with attainment or nonattainment conditions and convergent outer certificates.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames automated causal analysis as compilation from a query, assumptions, and observed information to a sharp mathematical answer, with point identification as a degenerate bound.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: realistic causal assumptions create idiosyncratic nonidentification -> hand derivation of sharp bounds does not scale -> compile the causal problem into polynomial optimization -> compute certified sharp ambiguity over a tied sparsest graph family

method_exemplars.technique: Polynomialize rational causal targets using auxiliary variables and prove equivalence between causal extrema and a constrained polynomial program solved with dual relaxation and spatial branch-and-bound.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The requested range is likewise an extremum of rational causal functionals over a semialgebraic discrete model, but its common-law constraints span several graphs.

method_exemplars.technique: Collapse represented DAGs into subclasses with distinct identified total-effect functionals before evaluating them.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Effect-functional quotienting can reduce the number of polynomial objectives whose joint sharp envelope must be computed.

method_exemplars.technique: Replace exact empirical cell constraints by simultaneous multinomial confidence regions and propagate those regions through the causal polynomial program.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sharp ambiguity bounds over tied graphs also require sampling uncertainty for estimated observed cells, separately from certificates controlling unfinished global optimization.

open_problems.open_problem: Can one construct uniformly valid selection-aware plug-in inference for a causal effect whose rational functional is certified common across all tied sparsest graph outputs, including local-to-zero CI signals and local-to-tie graph scores?

source_refs.claim: The paper obtains asymptotically valid post-discovery intervals by resampling PC conditional-independence statistics and unioning graphwise intervals, rather than exploiting a certified common multinomial rational functional.
source_refs.author: Ting-Hsuan Chang, Zijian Guo, Daniel Malinsky

source_refs.claim: The paper shows ordinary intervals can be invalid after reusing data for causal discovery and effect estimation and develops randomized-selection inference for a graph-selected target.
source_refs.author: Paula Gradu, Tijana Zrnic, Yixin Wang, Michael I. Jordan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Simultaneous identification is formulated at the population-density and candidate-graph level; the paper supplies no estimator, limit law, or post-discovery coverage theorem.
source_refs.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, Terry Soo
source_refs.venue: ICML 2025 Workshop on Scaling Up Intervention Models

open_problems.why_unsolved: A population equality certificate does not remove selection nonregularity: empirical CI decisions determine which minimum-edge graphs tie while the same cells estimate the common rational functional. Chang et al. protect the true effect by retaining and unioning graphwise intervals, while Gradu et al. target a learned-graph functional; neither exploits a proof that all retained graphs define one target. Near CI boundaries or sparsity-score ties, the selected family changes discontinuously, so a delta method conditional on the realized output is not uniform. The resampling proof must replace true-CPDAG containment with a simultaneous-functional stability event and control rational denominators near positivity boundaries.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An estimator with an asymptotic linear representation and an honest confidence set whose coverage is uniform over stated positive-cell and local-to-CI/local-to-tie regimes, plus either an efficiency characterization under stable common-effect certification or an impossibility theorem with a set-valued fallback under instability.

writing_exemplar.why: It separates uncertainty in causal discovery from uncertainty in effect estimation and targets coverage for a fixed causal effect rather than a selection-dependent projection.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: causal discovery chooses adjustment structure from the data -> reusing those data invalidates naive intervals -> resampling and graph screening recover coverage -> certified common identification may yield a less conservative honest interval across tied sparsest outputs

method_exemplars.technique: Perturb and resample intermediate CI statistics, screen candidate graphs, form graphwise regular estimators, and prove coverage through simultaneous retention of a causally valid graph.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The discovery stage is likewise CI-driven, while a common-effect certificate creates the possibility of replacing the final union by one pooled influence-function calculation.

method_exemplars.technique: Randomize score-based graph search, quantify selection stability, and transfer fixed-graph confidence guarantees to the selected target.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Sparsest-permutation and GSP families are search-selected, so the randomized-selection argument is a natural donor for local graph-tie instability.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct simultaneous confidence regions for multinomial observed cells and propagate them through rational or polynomial causal constraints.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The certified common functional is a rational function of the same finite probability table, making positivity-controlled cellwise inference the natural plug-in rung.

open_problems.open_problem: Does simultaneous causal-effect identification over a finite candidate set admit a necessary-and-sufficient graphical or graphical-algebraic criterion for arbitrary MPDAGs with semi-directed cycles, together with an identifying functional or a common-law nonidentifiability witness?

source_refs.claim: The paper explicitly limits its proof to SA-MPDAGs because it uses chain-graph results and states that general MPDAGs with semi-directed cycles require a different proof technique.
source_refs.author: Kai Z. Teh, Kayvan Sadeghi, Terry Soo
source_refs.venue: ICML 2025 Workshop on Scaling Up Intervention Models

source_refs.claim: For one arbitrary MPDAG, the paper provides a necessary-and-sufficient total-effect criterion and generalized truncated factorization, but not simultaneous identification across several non-equivalent MPDAGs.
source_refs.author: Emilija Perković

source_refs.claim: The paper gives a complete effect-identification algorithm and graphical nonidentifiability characterization for one PAG, not common-law equality across several candidate equivalence classes.
source_refs.author: Amin Jaber, Jiji Zhang, Elias Bareinboim

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest simultaneous-identification proof factorizes SA-MPDAGs as chain graphs and compares reduced ancestral chain graphs. Teh et al. explicitly state that semi-directed cycles in general MPDAGs invalidate that proof step. Perković resolves identification graph by graph, and Jaber et al. prove completeness for one PAG, but neither characterizes when their observable functionals agree on distributions common to several non-equivalent graph classes. A resolution requires a replacement for the chain-component comparison and a failure construction shared by the entire candidate set.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A necessary-and-sufficient criterion and terminating algorithm for finite sets of arbitrary MPDAGs that returns a common identifying functional when the criterion holds and otherwise returns a finite graphical obstruction plus a compatible positive distribution witnessing unequal interventions.

writing_exemplar.why: Its discussion names general MPDAGs as the immediate proof boundary and explains why the existing chain-graph argument stops there.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: background knowledge refines CPDAGs into MPDAGs -> several MPDAGs may remain plausible -> SA-MPDAG chain components permit a sufficient common-effect test -> remove the no-semi-directed-cycle restriction with a complete criterion

method_exemplars.technique: Use proper possibly causal paths and partial-causal-order bucket factorization to derive a necessary-and-sufficient graph-specific MPDAG identification formula.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A simultaneous criterion for general MPDAGs must reuse these complete single-graph functionals and then characterize their equality.

method_exemplars.technique: Apply a recursive identification algorithm over a partial graph and prove completeness by turning algorithmic failure into a graphical nonidentifiability construction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Its success-or-obstruction proof pattern is the closest established template for a common-functional-or-witness theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Estimate MPDAG-identified point or joint total effects by recursive least squares and prove efficiency among regular covariance-based estimators in linear causally sufficient models.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a concrete estimation rung after a multi-MPDAG criterion returns a shared functional, while clearly exposing the additional linearity restriction.

literature_map:
Raskutti and Uhler (2018, Stat) define sparsest-permutation discovery around minimum-edge permutation DAGs under the sparsest Markov representation assumption, without an effect-aware policy for cross-MEC ties.
Solus, Wang, and Uhler (2021, Biometrika) establish consistency guarantees for greedy permutation search, but the target remains graph recovery rather than common-effect recovery under ties.
Lam, Andrews, and Ramsey (2022, UAI) develop greedy relaxations of the sparsest-permutation algorithm, again without a common-effect-or-ambiguity output contract.
Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2024, arXiv:2408.07575) develop a general framework for constraint-based causal learning and emphasize that discovery may not yield a unique graphical representation.
Teh, Sadeghi, and Soo (2025, arXiv:2506.15561) introduce simultaneous identification beyond one MEC, prove a sufficient SA-MPDAG criterion, and explicitly leave necessity and general MPDAGs open.
Perković (2020, UAI; arXiv:1910.02997) gives a necessary-and-sufficient total-effect criterion and generalized truncated factorization for one MPDAG.
Guo and Perković (2021, AISTATS; arXiv:2010.08611) minimally enumerate distinct total-effect functionals inside one MPDAG, making effect quotienting preferable to raw DAG enumeration.
Jaber, Zhang, and Bareinboim (2019, ICML) give complete causal-effect identification and a graphical failure characterization for one PAG.
Wienöbst, Luttermann, Bannach, and Liśkiewicz (2023, AAAI; arXiv:2301.12212) give linear-delay DAG enumeration within MECs and MPDAGs with background knowledge, but do not quotient by effect equality.
Garcia, Stillman, and Sturmfels (2005, Journal of Symbolic Computation; arXiv:math/0301255) encode discrete Bayesian-network CI models as polynomial ideals and analyze their algebraic components.
Kang and Tian (2012, Polynomial Constraints in Causal Bayesian Networks) use implicitization to derive equality constraints under interventions, without solving common-law effect equality across candidate graphs.
Duarte, Finkelstein, Knox, Mummolo, and Shpitser (2024, JASA; arXiv:2109.13471) compile discrete causal queries into polynomial programs with sharp, anytime-valid, and epsilon-sharp bounds.
Guo and Perković (2022, JMLR; arXiv:2008.03481) give efficient recursive least squares for effects identified in one MPDAG under linearity and causal sufficiency.
Gradu, Zrnic, Wang, and Jordan (2025, JASA) show that post-discovery data reuse invalidates naive coverage and develop randomized-selection inference for learned graph functionals.
Chang, Guo, and Malinsky (2024, arXiv:2405.06763) obtain fixed-effect coverage by resampling PC decisions and unioning graphwise intervals, leaving open inference that exploits a certified common functional across tied sparsest outputs.
